question: Does floral phenotype converge on one universal island syndrome, or remain contingent on pollinator architecture, colonization filtering, climate and island context?
prediction_from_current_hypothesis: If pollination function recurs but interaction architecture diverges, floral traits should show structured but non-universal responses: local matching, transitional phenotypes, filtering and context dependence rather than one globally directional island syndrome.

studies.design: 16 floral morphology/nectar traits in 26 native species plus bird and insect visitation frequency
studies.result: Bird-associated plants tended toward bell-shaped white flowers, wider corollas at nectary level and more nectar, while insect-associated plants tended toward bowl/tubular flowers, narrower corollas and less nectar. Bird-visited flowers nevertheless showed mixed traits and did not fit a classical ornithophilous syndrome.

studies.design: Community-wide floral traits and visitors across 12 islands; 269 native flowering plants
studies.result: Small, subdued and accessible flowers were common with generalist visitors, but specialized niches with vivid, large or deep flowers persisted for birds, long-proboscis moths and carpenter bees.

studies.design: Island-mainland comparison of selfing capacity, floral morphology, hummingbird visitation and selection
studies.result: Island plants had higher capacity for self-pollination, but current island pollinator service was not lower or more variable and current selection for selfing was not detected; island-mainland corolla divergence also lacked consistent evidence of present pollinator-mediated selection.

studies.design: 556 plant species; 136 phylogenetically independent island-mainland sister-taxon contrasts
studies.result: Flowers were not smaller on islands on average. Galapagos and Revillagigedo showed smaller island flowers, but direction varied among archipelagos and plant families, including larger, smaller and no-change responses.

studies.design: >2500 angiosperm species across 14 islands and 400-m elevation bands using Bayesian phylogenetic occurrence models
studies.result: All six flower traits varied with combinations of temperature, precipitation seasonality, island area and isolation; climate best predicted some traits whereas island characteristics better predicted others.

studies.design: Oceanic-island community comparison of floral traits, visitor functional groups and ecological specialization
studies.result: Plants received more pollinator species than classical syndromes predicted; five floral traits explained only 22.5% of visitation preference, although restrictive flowers were more specialized than unrestrictive flowers.

strongest_current_reading: Distant island floras repeatedly preserve pollination function, but floral phenotypes do not converge on one universal island form. Trait responses track a mixture of local interaction architecture, colonization filtering, climate, island area/isolation and historical partner turnover. This is the morphology-level counterpart of functional recurrence plus architectural divergence.
claim_boundary: The studies use different trait sets and designs, so this screen tests directional consistency and explanatory structure, not a common standardized morphology effect size.
